title: Better answers, broader thinking: What students gain from ChatGPT and critical-thinking training
institution: Bocconi University, in collaboration with OpenAI Economic Research
finding: In a randomised experiment with more than 1,000 first-year undergraduates assigned to ChatGPT access (GPT-4o), causal-reasoning training, both, or neither, students given ChatGPT access scored almost a full point higher on a five-point human-graded rubric and produced work more similar to expert-written recommendations.

title: Better answers, broader thinking: What students gain from ChatGPT and critical-thinking training
institution: Bocconi University, in collaboration with OpenAI Economic Research
finding: Causal-reasoning training raised the originality and variety of student ideas but produced no gain on the grading rubric, which measured only how well recommendations addressed two marketing goals - a documented measurement-instrument blind spot showing that conventional rubrics can miss originality once AI makes polished output cheap.

title: DSRI Newsletter Volume 1
institution: UL Research Institutes - Digital Safety Research Institute (DSRI)
finding: At DEF CON 2025, deepfake detection analytics developed on the DARPA SemaFor program detected advanced attendee-generated deepfakes with only 43% accuracy; in a separate real-versus-fake image game using open-source generators, SemaFor was correct 93% of the time against 77% for ~5,000 human guesses.
